title: Tutorial Sheet: Unit 2 – Sessions 1, 2 & 3 (Sections A & B)
sections: 1. Four main functional units: Input Unit, Output Unit, Memory Unit, and CPU (Arithmetic Logic Unit + Control Unit).
2. Control Unit: coordinates and controls all other units — it fetches and decodes instructions and issues timing/control signals that execute them.
3. Bus: a shared communication pathway (set of lines) that transfers data, addresses and control signals between CPU, memory and I/O devices.
4. ALU: the Arithmetic Logic Unit — the part of the CPU that performs arithmetic (add, subtract) and logic (AND, OR, compare) operations.
5. Address bus is used to transfer memory addresses.

1. Data Bus carries actual data between units (bidirectional); Address Bus carries the location/address of the data (unidirectional, CPU → memory); Control Bus carries command and timing signals such as Read, Write and Interrupt.
2. Program Counter: holds the address of the next instruction; during fetch its value goes to the MAR, then it auto-increments (or is set by a branch) so instructions execute in sequence.
3. Steps for Load R2, LOC: (i) PC → MAR, instruction fetched to IR, PC incremented; (ii) instruction decoded; (iii) address field LOC → MAR, memory read; (iv) data → MDR; (v) MDR → R2.
4. Limitations of single bus: only one transfer at a time (serialized), bus contention slows the system, performance limited by bus speed, a bus fault can halt the whole system.
5. Advantages: simple/low cost, easy to connect devices. Disadvantages: slower due to sharing, not suitable for high-performance systems with many transfers.
